paper_metadata.title: High temperature deformation behaviors of a high Nb containing TiAl alloy

evidence.quote: In the present paper, high temperature tensile and creep behaviors of Ti e45Ale9(Nb,W,B,Y) alloy with duplex (DP) microstructure were investigated.

and remelted in a vacuum-skull melting furnace in order to reduce composition heterogeneity
An ingot with dimension of F 120 /C2 240 mm was prepared by casting into a graphite mould.
Then the ingot was hot isostatic pressed (HIP) under an argon pressure of 140 MPa for 4 h to eliminate casting porosity.
A DP microstructure was obtained by canned forging the ingot at temperature above 1100 /C14 C followed by air cooling to room temperature.

evidence.quote: After creep, ﬁne equiaxed grains form both at the gauge section and the threaded section. The size of the new-formed grains is about 0.5 e3 mm.

EDS analysis indicates that the white small grains consist of Ti 51 at.%, Nb 10 at.% and Al 39 at.%. The stoichiometric ratio between Ti þ Nb and Al is 3:1, suggesting that the bright phase is a2 phase.
Some of the equiaxed grains aggregate, showing the spheroidization of lamellar plates during high temperature deformation.
For the specimen tensiled at 1 /C2 10 /C0 4 s/C0 1, g and a2/g lamellae elongate along tensile direction and the cavities form on some grain boundaries.

The main reason for the higher high temperature strength comes from the Nb and W additions, which are found to strengthen but also embrittle the g phase.

The strengthening effect of W addition is thought to be associated with lamellar width reﬁnement and solid solution, which is induced by W, that impedes elevated temperature dislocation movement [12].
During creep or tension at low strain rates, the alloy is susceptible to colony (or grain) boundary sliding (GBS), which leads to a high elongation.
It is assumed that the diffusion-assisted climb of dislocations might be the controlling mechanism at the minimum creep rate stage.
